text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, which forces the right side of the heart to work harder.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

text_blocks.snippet: In the early stages, PAH often causes no noticeable symptoms. When signs do appear, they frequently mimic other heart or lung conditions:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea) during everyday activities like walking or climbing stairs
Heart palpitations or a racing, pounding heartbeat

text_blocks.snippet: As the condition progresses and the right side of the heart begins to strain or fail, more severe symptoms develop:

list.snippet: Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting (syncope), especially during physical exertion
Swelling (edema) in the ankles, legs, feet, or abdomen
Bluish or gray lips and skin (cyanosis)
Coughing up blood (hemoptysis) in rare or advanced cases
Voice hoarseness caused by an enlarged pulmonary artery pressing on a nerve

text_blocks.snippet: Learn more about tracking and diagnosing these signs through the American Lung Association.
If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, let me know:

list.snippet: Who is having these symptoms (age, general health)?
How long have the symptoms been happening, or do they happen mainly during exercise?
